root_cause_label: Speech-to-Text Tool Applied to Silent Visual-Text Video
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent chose Whisper (automatic speech recognition) to extract text from a silent Zork screen-recording where all content is displayed visually, then looped through multiple Whisper model sizes (tiny, base, small) and audio extraction variants without ever pivoting to OCR-based frame extraction.
t_err_evidence: In step 1 the agent's analysis states it will install 'whisper' to transcribe the video, planning 'My first step is to install all the necessary packages from the apt package manager... This includes updating the package list and then installing yt-dlp, ffmpeg, and python3-pip. This is an efficient way to set up the environment' — the fundamental error of choosing an ASR tool for a visual-only video is made here before any exploration of the video content.
t_commit_evidence: From step 1, the agent commits fully to the ASR/Whisper pipeline across all remaining 29 steps; it installs openai-whisper (steps 4-9), downloads the video (steps 9-14), and runs Whisper exclusively (steps 15-29) without ever considering OCR or frame-level extraction, making the failing outcome locked in from the first decision.
t_surface_evidence: Step 17 shows the first Whisper result: '[00:00.000 --> 00:02.000] You ... [03:08.000 --> 03:10.000] You' — the transcript contains only repeated 'You' tokens, providing the first observable signal that the approach cannot extract the required Zork moves.
trigger_explanation: The agent operated on the unverified assumption that the Zork gameplay video contained meaningful speech audio that could be transcribed. Zork is a text-based game; the screen-recording shows only visual text on screen with no meaningful spoken dialogue. The agent never inspected the video's audio track or considered that the content was purely visual before committing to an ASR pipeline.
